FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing was run).

## RQ and falsifiable claims
RQ: Do the labels cleaned by Docta demonstrate higher credibility—reflected in improved predictive performance—compared to raw labels, validated by ChatGPT and in-house human annotators on the disagreement subset?

We commit to TWO separable, pre-registered claims:
- C1 (primary, performance): A downstream predictor trained on Docta-cleaned labels achieves at least Δ*=2.0 absolute percentage points (pp) higher held-out test accuracy than the same predictor trained on raw labels, and the difference is statistically significant.
- C2 (corroborative, label-level): On the disagreement subset, arbitration (human majority + single ChatGPT verdict) sides with the Docta label significantly more often than chance, and arbiter verdicts agree with the gold label at a rate far above the raw-label error rate.

Refinement 2 (no confounding feedback) is honored by construction: arbitration verdicts are NEVER folded into the training labels of the A-vs-B model that underpins C1. They feed only (i) the corroborative C2 analysis on a separate audit split and (ii) an explicitly separate third "adjudicated-label" condition (CondC) that tests the feedback path directly.

## 1. Gold-label sourcing (pinned decision, refinement 1)
We use a REAL curated gold test set layered on top of a CONTROLLED synthetic noise scheme, so credibility is measured against provable ground truth.
- Base: public IMDb sentiment (25k train / 25k test), clean curated labels, binary, class-balanced, CPU-friendly text. (Hard prerequisite: cache the dataset, since environment.datasets=[], network disabled; the design requires it to be staged before execution.)
- Fixed stratified split of the 25k train pool BEFORE any corruption: TR_train n=14,000 | TR_audit n=4,000 | TR_val n=3,000 | TE_gold n=4,000. TE_gold is QUARANTINED from the start: no instance/label from it ever reaches Docta, arbiters, or model training; it is used only for the headline evaluation.
- Raw label set = clean labels corrupted by a pre-registered noise model: symmetric class-flip with flip probability τ=0.25 (each label independently flipped with prob τ, seeded RNG). Sensitivity sweep τ∈{0.10,0.25,0.40} and an asymmetric variant (p(flip 0→1)=0.4, p(1→0)=0.1) is a pre-registered secondary analysis, NOT the headline.
- Gold ground truth is therefore known at label level (clean labels) and at test level (TE_gold). Clean-gold test split generation: fixed stratified random split with fixed seed, computed once before any downstream work.

## 2. Docta and downstream predictor (both pinned)
- Docta: black-box label-cleaning component. Input: TR_train + TR_audit instances with their raw (corrupted) labels and features only. Output: cleaned labels (± confidence), separately for TR_train and TR_audit. Docta NEVER sees TR_val, TE_gold, or any gold labels. Version/release and random seed are pinned and recorded (exact snapshot required if a real implementation is used).
- Predictor (identical across conditions): L2-regularized logistic regression on TF-IDF features (unigram+bigram, 50k features, max_df=0.8, min_df=2), C=1.0, fixed iteration budget (no label-conditional early stopping), class-balanced. Hyperparameters frozen a priori. This choice keeps compute feasible on the declared CPU-only, 224-core environment; a transformer variant is noted as optional future work if GPU becomes available.

## 3. Conditions
- CondA (raw): model trained on raw (corrupted) train labels.
- CondB (Docta): model trained on Docta-cleaned train labels.  ← THE comparison (A vs B) is the sole basis for C1.
- CondC (adjudicated, explicit third condition per refinement 2): TR_train disputes (raw≠Docta) relabeled via the arbitration decision rule; non-disputed instances keep the label (raw=Docta by definition); unresolved disputes keep the raw label (conservative). CondC tests whether folding adjudicated labels back actually helps (C vs B, C vs A); it is a separate sub-question and does not enter C1.

## 4. Arbitration protocol (pinned, strictly corroborative)
- Dispute definition: per instance, Docta label ≠ raw label.
- Venues: (a) TR_audit disputes — adjudicated but NEVER used to train any model; this is the source of the C2 corroborative evidence; (b) TR_train disputes — adjudicated ONLY to construct CondC labels.
- Human panel: N_h=5 in-house annotators, each independently classifies every audit dispute and each TR_train dispute, BLIND to provenance (shown only the review text; asked for the correct class, not to "side" with either set), to prevent anchoring.
- ChatGPT: one fixed model/version, pre-registered prompt (single uniform template), temperature=0, 3 repeated calls per instance with the majority of the 3 taken as the ChatGPT verdict (self-consistency); reproducibility pinned via prompt + model version + seed.
- Decision rule (pre-registered): adjudicated label requires human majority (≥3 of 5) AND ChatGPT agreement with that majority. Otherwise the instance is "unresolved" (excluded from C2 success counts as unresolved; keeps raw label in CondC). Human-majority vs ChatGPT cross-agreement is reported as a reliability statistic (not as the truth).
- Arbitration quality is additionally evaluated against gold: arbiter verdicts on TR_audit are scored for accuracy vs the known clean labels — a direct "did arbitration validate the right label" check independent of model training.

## 5. Analysis plan (pre-registration per refinement 3)
Primary metric: held-out test accuracy on TE_gold (balanced binary, so accuracy is appropriate); secondary: macro-F1, log-loss.
Pre-registered decision thresholds:
- H0 (one-sided): Docta-trained accuracy ≤ raw-trained accuracy; H1: >. α=0.05 (directional per the RQ), with two-sided 95% CI on the accuracy difference also reported.
- Minimum material effect: Δ* = +2.0 pp absolute (meaningful vs the 25% injected noise; a claim requires BOTH significance AND Δ ≥ Δ*).
- Sample size / power: TE_gold n=4,000 gives SE(diff) ≤ ~1.1 pp even at worst-case within-subject correlation; power > 0.9 for Δ=2pp at α=0.05. This is the stated power rationale; the sample-size target is n_te=4,000.
- Seed aggregation: 5 independent data-generation seeds × 5 model seeds = 25 runs/condition. Report mean ± SD of Δ across runs; per-example McNemar test on each seed; combine via meta-analysis (Stouffer) and report the distribution of Δ. Success rule for C1 (pre-registered): Δ ≥ Δ* AND significant at α=0.05 in ≥4 of 5 data-seeds; otherwise "not demonstrated".
- Corroborative C2 tests: binomial test on the TR_audit disputes for P(adjudicated label = Docta label | dispute) > 0.5 (α=0.05), plus arbiter-vs-gold accuracy and label-noise rates (fraction of raw vs Docta labels differing from gold on audit). C2 is supportive, not sufficient (C1 remains the credibility arbiter).
- Sensitivities (secondary, pre-registered): τ sweep {0.10,0.25,0.40} and asymmetric noise for A vs B; CondC vs A and B.
- Controls: identical splits/features/hyperparameters/training budget across conditions (only training labels differ); quarantined gold test; seeded Docta; blind arbitration with no provenance leakage; all thresholds fixed before any headline evaluation.

## 6. Feasibility / budget (stated as constraints, not executed)
- Data prerequisite: IMDb must be staged locally (empty environment.datasets, no network); a small held-out sanity subset should be used first as an exploratory check (successful exploration ≠ completed experiment).
- Compute: CPU-only, 224 cores. TF-IDF + logistic regression: minutes per fit; 25 runs/condition × (A,B,C) ≈ 75 fits plus τ-sweep — comfortably feasible. No GPU required; transformer variant deferred.
- Annotation: human cost scales with disputes. At τ=0.25 on 18k train+audit instances, ~4,500 instances are flips; if Docta relabels perfectly the disputes ≈ #flips ≈ 4,500 → 5 judges × 4,500 ≈ 22,500 human judgments (blinding/QC overhead extra). If Docta is imperfect, disputes are larger; a dispute cap (e.g., adjudicate a pre-specified random sample of up to 1,500 audit disputes for C2, and up to 2,000 for CondC) is set to bound cost, with sampling done once pre-registration.
- ChatGPT cost: 3 calls × (capped disputes) ≈ 10.5k calls, all short prompts — within a modest budget; feasibility is documented as an assumption, not a guarantee.
- Risk mitigations: dispute caps, pre-registered success rules, quarantine discipline, and seed aggregation all reduce the chance of an under-powered or confounded verdict.

## 7. Deliverable evidence package
Pre-registration sheet (metrics, Δ*, α, success rule, splits, seeds, prompts, decision rule) BEFORE any evaluation; the 25 runs' accuracy matrix by condition; McNemar/bootstrap CIs; TR_audit arbitration tally (sides-with-Docta rate, arbiter-vs-gold accuracy, human–ChatGPT agreement); CondC comparison; τ-sensitivity; and a clearly labeled "no experiment was executed; this is a design" disclosure.
